title: "quarto-index principal-mention regressions"
from: markdown-smart
format:
  pdf:
    # The `.ilg` is this fixture's evidence that none of the shapes below draws
    # a makeindex warning, and the `.ind`/`.aux` are what the expected printed
    # index is derived FROM; Quarto deletes all three on a successful render
    # unless this says otherwise.
    latex-clean: false
    include-in-header:
      # The author redefinition, which the extension documents, and which is
      # also the only way the emphasis becomes visible to `pdftotext` at all:
      # `\textbf` and plain text extract identically. Every emphasis claim this
      # fixture makes is read through this marker.
      #
      # `\newcommand*`, and not `\renewcommand*`: Quarto puts a document's own
      # header text ABOVE what a filter injects, so this definition lands first
      # and the extension's `\providecommand` steps aside — which is what
      # README's "yours is kept" means, and what this render exercises.
      # `\renewcommand*` here fails outright, the command not existing yet.
      text: |
        \newcommand*\quartoindexprincipal[1]{[P:#1]}
filters:
  - index

# A plain and a principal mark of one key on one page

This is the shape the milestone died on, and it is here forever (IP2). Before
the typeset-time channel, the plain mark emitted a bare `\index` command and
the principal one an encapsulated command, which makeindex refuses to reconcile
when the two share a page: it warns, and Quarto fails the render on that
warning. Now every locator of the key carries the same encapsulation, so there
is nothing left to conflict, and the two marks fold into one locator that the
registry then emphasizes.

A passing mention of [wyvern]{.index} and, in the same sentence and on the same
page, its principal discussion: [wyvern]{.index mention="principal"}.

{{< pagebreak >}}

A second passing mention of [wyvern]{.index}, a page later, which must stay
plain.

# A principal mark inside a footnote

A footnote's `\index` command is written by the same deferred-to-shipout
mechanism the registration uses, so the two name the same page even though the
mark is typeset in a different box from the one it was written in.[^naga]

[^naga]: The principal discussion of [naga]{.index mention="principal"} lives in
    this note.

{{< pagebreak >}}

# A registered page folded inside a makeindex range

makeindex folds three or more consecutive pages under one encapsulation into a
range, and the registry looks a page up by the string the index prints, which a
range does not match. So this term's principal page prints unemphasized — the
one silent degradation this back-end has, documented in README and left to M21,
which is where page ranges are taken up.

The first mention: [oni]{.index}.

{{< pagebreak >}}

The principal discussion, on the next page: [oni]{.index mention="principal"}.

{{< pagebreak >}}

The last mention, on the page after that: [oni]{.index}.

{{< pagebreak >}}

# A range whose FIRST page is the registered one

The same fold, with the principal mark at the head of the run rather than
inside it. This one is here because a locator command that split its page list
wrongly could still emphasize this entry — the range string begins with the
registered page's own digits — while emphasizing nothing else. It must print
exactly as plain as the entry above.

The principal discussion first: [sylph]{.index mention="principal"}.

{{< pagebreak >}}

Then [sylph]{.index},

{{< pagebreak >}}

and [sylph]{.index} again.

{{< pagebreak >}}

# A registered page that is not the first item of its list

Two mentions on non-adjacent pages, so makeindex writes two locators rather
than one range, and the principal one is the SECOND. A locator command that
read only the head of what it was handed would emphasize neither.

A passing mention: [troll]{.index}.

{{< pagebreak >}}

The principal discussion, two pages on: [troll]{.index mention="principal"}.

{{< pagebreak >}}

# A page number of more than one character

Everything above sits in single digits. This term's only mention is past page
nine, so its page number is two tokens rather than one — the shape that read a
page list one token at a time got wrong, printing the first digit inside the
locator and the rest outside it, emphasized by nothing and linked to nothing.

The principal and only discussion of [undine]{.index mention="principal"}.

# A cross-reference that only becomes a self-reference after the fold

The LaTeX back-end stores three levels and folds anything deeper into the
third. This mark's target differs from its entry as the author wrote them, so
nothing drops it before the back-end branch; the fold then rewrites the entry
to exactly what the target names, and the target is dropped as a
self-reference. The mark therefore DOES contribute a locator, and its role
applies. Telling it otherwise first — that a cross-reference had taken its
locator's place — would contradict the drop's own report a line later, which is
the defect this milestone was returned for once already.

[vodyanoy]{.index entry="deep!water!folk!kin" mention="principal" see="deep!water!folk, kin"}

{{< pagebreak >}}

# The control this fixture must leave alone

A term with no role anywhere, marked twice: [pixie]{.index} here,

{{< pagebreak >}}

and [pixie]{.index} a page later. Neither locator may be marked, and the
document may carry no registration for it at all.
